name: basic-tools-surface
description: read(path,offset,limit,display), edit(ops[]), write(ops[]), grep(pattern,path,type,hidden,max_depth,display), find(ops[]), ls(path,recursive,display), shell(command,timeout,env,readonlyShell), ast_search(query,path,language,glob,limit,display), revert_file(path,checkpoint_id?). All in basic-tools extension. No bash tool (remove-bash hook removes it).

name: context-tools-surface
description: ctx_record(content,tags?,anchor?), ctx_packet(query?,format?), ctx_inject(content,at?). Context extension. Ephemeral session injection layer — distinct from grove (grove=persistent semantic store, context=session scratchpad/injection).

name: shell-nushell-syntax
description: Shell tool executes Nushell NOT POSIX/bash. Forbidden patterns: 2>/dev/null, 2>&1, &&, ||, $(), backticks. Nu equivalents: out+err>| for redirect, ; for sequence, prefix external binary with ^ if shadowed by Nu builtin (e.g. ^ls). POSIX idioms silently fail or produce wrong output in Nu.

content: Extensions Architecture: basic-tools & context runtime patterns. basic-tools dispatches an Op[] discriminated union schema (read, grep, edit, write, find, ls, shell, ast_search) using linehash (xxhash32 4-char hex anchors) for anchored diffs and fuzzy edit matching, with TOON structural encoding for 30-50% token reduction over JSON. shell uses Nushell syntax. context provides ephemeral session scratchpads (ctx_record, ctx_packet, ctx_inject) separate from persistent grove storage. Planned extensions (extra-tools, grove, quality-stack, docs-tools, web-tools) will follow this non-colliding Op[] or scoped tool convention.

title: Single Tool Pattern (sh) and Container-Aware Sandboxing
rationale: Bespoke JSON tools consume 3k-8k tokens in system prompts and bottleneck reasoning on small local models. Nushell provides typed pipelines and loops natively. Running nested bwrap inside rootless containers fails or adds pointless overhead, whereas host runs require it for protection.
